scenario: 自动驾驶车(AV)每 100ms 要出一次决策，目标检测器跑在车载 Jetson 边缘硬件上，行人和骑车人是安全攸关目标。
scenario_en: An autonomous vehicle (AV) must decide every 100ms, its object detector runs on an on-board Jetson edge box, and pedestrians and cyclists are safety-critical targets.
q: 边缘目标检测的核心权衡轴是什么？
q_en: What is the central tradeoff axis for edge object detection?
why: 核心轴是准确率(mAP) vs 边缘硬件上的推理延迟：一个 COCO 榜单第一但在 Jetson 上只有 2 FPS 的模型来不及刹车，一个超快但漏检小孩的模型会出人命。两头都不能要，要在这条轴上找够快又不漏关键目标的点。
why_en: The axis is accuracy (mAP) versus inference latency on edge hardware: a SOTA-mAP model at 2 FPS on a Jetson brakes too late, and an ultra-fast model that misses a child kills someone, so you tune for fast-enough-without-missing.
diagram:
flowchart TB A["高 mAP 但 2 FPS on Jetson
决策太慢"] --> C{"边缘权衡
准确率 vs 延迟"} B["超快但漏检行人
安全事故"] --> C C --> G["可用检测器
够快 + 不漏关键目标"]
options: 只看 COCO 榜单 mAP，越高越安全，延迟不是检测器选型该操心的事
准确率(mAP) vs 边缘硬件推理延迟的权衡：既要够快出决策，又不能漏检安全攸关目标
只看 FPS，速度越快越好，准确率可以为吞吐让路，速度是唯一硬约束
只需在云端 GPU 上把吞吐做满，车载边缘硬件的算力不影响架构选择
options_en: Only look at COCO mAP — higher is safer, and latency is not something detector selection should worry about.
Accuracy (mAP) versus edge inference latency: fast enough to decide in time, yet never missing a safety-critical object.
Only look at FPS — faster is always better, and accuracy can yield to throughput since speed is the sole hard constraint.
Just maximize throughput on cloud GPUs; the on-board edge box's compute does not affect architecture choice.
optionExplanations: 只追 mAP 会选出在 Jetson 上跑不动的模型，2 FPS = 每帧 500ms，AV 的 100ms 预算直接爆掉。
对；两个失败方向(太慢、漏检)都致命，所以设计从一开始就是这条准确率-延迟轴上的约束优化。
只追速度会漏检行人，一次漏检就是一条人命，速度不能是唯一约束。
检测器跑在车上，云端吞吐救不了车载延迟，边缘硬件的算力和访存正是约束来源。
optionExplanations_en: Chasing only mAP picks a model that can't run on Jetson — 2 FPS means 500ms per frame, blowing the AV's 100ms budget.
Correct — both failure directions (too slow, missed detection) are fatal, so the design is a constrained optimization on this accuracy-latency axis from the start.
Chasing only speed misses pedestrians, and one miss is a life, so speed cannot be the only constraint.
The detector runs on the car; cloud throughput can't fix on-board latency, and the edge hardware's compute and memory are the constraint.

termDefinitions.meaning: 目标检测的主指标：对所有类别、多个 IoU 阈值求平均精度，衡量检测又准又全的程度。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: mAP (mean Average Precision) is the main detection metric, averaging precision across classes and IoU thresholds to measure how accurately and completely a model detects objects.

termDefinitions.meaning: 自动驾驶车辆，检测器在车载算力上实时运行。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: AV (Autonomous Vehicle) is a self-driving car whose detector must run in real time on on-board compute.

termDefinitions.meaning: NVIDIA 的边缘 GPU 模块，常用作车载/嵌入式 AI 推理硬件。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Jetson is NVIDIA's edge GPU module, commonly used as on-board or embedded AI inference hardware.

termDefinitions.meaning: 每秒处理的帧数，2 FPS 即每帧耗时 500ms。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: FPS (Frames Per Second) is how many frames are processed per second; 2 FPS means 500ms per frame.

q: 把边缘目标检测优化拆成四大支柱，哪个选项完整列全了？
q_en: Which option lists all four pillars of optimizing edge object detection?
why: 四大支柱是:架构族选型、压缩(剪枝+量化)、硬件感知 NAS、置信度校准。它们分别管:选哪种模型、怎么把模型压小压快、让搜索算法替你挑架构、以及让置信度可信到能支撑 fail-safe。
why_en: The four pillars are architecture families, compression (pruning plus quantization), hardware-aware NAS, and confidence calibration — covering which model, how to shrink and speed it, letting search pick the architecture, and making confidence trustworthy enough for fail-safe.
options: 架构族选型、压缩(剪枝+量化)、硬件感知 NAS、置信度校准
数据增强、迁移学习、超参搜索、L2 正则化
架构族选型、压缩、分布式训练调度、云端 A/B 测试
换更大的 backbone、提高输入分辨率、增加 anchor、加深 FPN
options_en: Architecture families, compression (pruning + quantization), hardware-aware NAS, confidence calibration.
Data augmentation, transfer learning, hyperparameter search, L2 regularization.
Architecture families, compression, distributed training orchestration, cloud A/B testing.
Swap in a bigger backbone, raise input resolution, add more anchors, deepen the FPN.
optionExplanations: 对;这四条正好覆盖选型、压缩、自动搜索、可信度,是本课组织边缘优化的主线。
这些是通用训练技巧,不针对'边缘延迟 vs 准确率'这条主轴,漏了压缩、NAS、校准。
分布式训练和云端 A/B 是训练/上线基建,不是把模型塞进车载边缘的手段,替换掉了 NAS 和校准。
这些做法只会把模型做得更大更慢,和边缘约束背道而驰,不是优化支柱。
optionExplanations_en: Correct — these four cover selection, compression, automated search, and trustworthiness, the backbone of edge optimization here.
These are generic training tricks, not aimed at the edge latency-vs-accuracy axis, and they drop compression, NAS, and calibration.
Distributed training and cloud A/B are training/rollout infra, not ways to fit a model onto an on-board box, replacing NAS and calibration.
These only make the model bigger and slower, opposite to the edge constraint, so they are not optimization pillars.

termDefinitions.meaning: 神经架构搜索:用搜索算法自动找网络结构,而不是人手工设计。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: NAS (Neural Architecture Search) uses a search algorithm to automatically find network architectures instead of hand-designing them.

termDefinitions.meaning: 检测器的主干特征提取网络,通常是一个 CNN。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The backbone is the detector's main feature-extraction network, usually a CNN.

termDefinitions.meaning: 特征金字塔网络:融合不同尺度特征以检测大小不一的目标。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: FPN (Feature Pyramid Network) fuses features at multiple scales to detect objects of varying sizes.

scenario: 某检测器在 Jetson 上跑 2 FPS,而这辆 AV 要求每 100ms 出一次感知决策。
scenario_en: A detector runs at 2 FPS on Jetson, while the AV requires a perception decision every 100ms.
q: 2 FPS 对 100ms 决策预算意味着什么设计含义？
q_en: What design implication does 2 FPS carry for a 100ms decision budget?
why: FPS = Frames Per Second,2 FPS 即每帧 1000/2 = 500ms。100ms 是给定的 SLO 目标(不是公式推出来的),500ms 比它慢 5 倍,车看到行人时已经开过去了。含义:这个模型直接出局,必须靠压缩/换架构/NAS 把每帧压到 100ms 内。
why_en: FPS is frames per second, so 2 FPS is 1000/2 = 500ms per frame; against the given 100ms SLO that's 5x too slow, so this model is out and you must compress, swap architecture, or NAS it under 100ms per frame.
options: 500ms/帧,正好卡在 100ms 预算边缘,微调一下超参就能达标
2 FPS 说明吞吐足够,瓶颈只在准确率,延迟不用管
每帧 500ms,是 100ms 预算的 5 倍,模型直接出局,得靠压缩/换架构把每帧压进 100ms
FPS 越低反而延迟越低,2 FPS 其实比 30 FPS 更适合实时决策
options_en: 500ms per frame sits right at the 100ms budget, so a bit of hyperparameter tuning meets it.
2 FPS means throughput is plenty and the only bottleneck is accuracy, so latency can be ignored.
500ms per frame is 5x the 100ms budget, so the model is out and must be compressed or swapped to fit each frame under 100ms.
Lower FPS means lower latency, so 2 FPS is actually better for real-time decisions than 30 FPS.

termDefinitions.meaning: 服务级目标,这里指'每 100ms 出一次决策'这类给定的延迟指标,不是算出来的。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An SLO (Service Level Objective) is a target such as 'a decision every 100ms', a given latency requirement rather than a derived number.

termDefinitions.meaning: 每秒处理的帧数,2 FPS = 每帧 500ms。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: FPS (Frames Per Second) is frames processed per second; 2 FPS equals 500ms per frame.

optionExplanations: 500ms 是 100ms 预算的 5 倍,并非'卡在边缘',微调超参救不了这么大的差距。
FPS 只反映速度,不能证明吞吐'足够',而且这款检测器早在延迟这关就没通过。
对;500ms 远超预算 5 倍,这个模型跑不动,得靠压缩或换架构才能把每帧塞进 100ms。
FPS 越低意味着每帧越慢,是延迟更差,不是更低,这个说法把方向弄反了。
optionExplanations_en: 500ms is 5x the 100ms budget, not 'right at the edge' — no amount of hyperparameter tweaking closes a gap that size.
FPS alone doesn't prove throughput is fine, and this detector already fails the latency gate before accuracy even comes up.
Correct — 500ms blows the budget by 5x, so the model can't run, and it needs compression or a different architecture to hit the 100ms-per-frame target.
Lower FPS means each frame takes longer, i.e. worse latency, not lower — this has the direction backwards.

q: YOLO 系列是怎么做到边缘上超低延迟的？
q_en: How does the YOLO family achieve ultra-low latency on the edge?
why: YOLO = You Only Look Once,单阶段检测:整张图一次 CNN 前向就同时出框和类别,没有两阶段的区域提议环节。YOLOv5/v8 用 anchor-free 头,边缘 GPU 上可到 sub-10ms;代价是对小目标和被遮挡目标较弱。
why_en: YOLO (You Only Look Once) is single-stage: one CNN forward pass over the whole image predicts boxes and classes at once, with no separate region-proposal stage, and v5/v8 use anchor-free heads to hit sub-10ms on edge GPUs at the cost of weaker small or occluded objects.
options: 两阶段:先跑区域提议网络选候选框,再逐框分类,所以精度高但延迟低
把图切成很多小块,每块单独跑一个大模型,再投票聚合结果
单阶段:整张图一次 CNN 前向同时出框和类别,anchor-free 头,边缘上 sub-10ms
纯 Transformer 注意力全局建模,天生适合边缘的低延迟场景
options_en: Two-stage: run a region-proposal network for candidate boxes, then classify each box, giving high accuracy and low latency.
Split the image into many patches, run a large model on each patch, then vote to aggregate.
Single-stage: one CNN forward pass over the whole image predicts boxes and classes at once with anchor-free heads, hitting sub-10ms on the edge.
Pure Transformer attention with global modeling, naturally suited to low-latency edge scenarios.
optionExplanations: 两阶段(如 Faster R-CNN)恰恰因为多一步区域提议而更慢,YOLO 的卖点正是省掉它。
分块跑大模型会成倍增加计算,和 YOLO 的单次前向低延迟相反。
对;一次前向 = 一次算完,anchor-free 又省掉 anchor 匹配,这是它 sub-10ms 的根源。
纯 Transformer(DETR)延迟高、访存大,是边缘上最不适合的一类,不是 YOLO。
optionExplanations_en: Two-stage detectors like Faster R-CNN are slower precisely because of the extra proposal step, which YOLO's whole pitch is to drop.
Running a large model per patch multiplies compute, the opposite of YOLO's single low-latency forward pass.
Correct — one forward pass computes everything, and anchor-free removes anchor matching, which is the root of its sub-10ms.
Pure Transformers (DETR) have high latency and memory and are the worst fit for the edge, not YOLO.

termDefinitions.meaning: 单阶段检测器,整张图一次前向同时预测框和类别。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: YOLO (You Only Look Once) is a single-stage detector that predicts boxes and classes in one forward pass over the whole image.

termDefinitions.meaning: 不预设一堆候选框(anchor),直接回归目标框,省掉锚框匹配这步。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Anchor-free heads regress boxes directly instead of matching against a preset grid of anchor boxes, removing the anchor-matching step.

termDefinitions.meaning: 一次前向就出最终检测,不做单独的区域提议阶段。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Single-stage means the final detections come from one forward pass, with no separate region-proposal stage.

q: EfficientDet 靠什么在中等延迟下拿到更强的小目标检测？
q_en: What lets EfficientDet get stronger small-object detection at moderate latency?
why: 两件东西:BiFPN(双向特征金字塔)做多尺度双向特征融合,让高层语义和低层细节互相流动,利于小目标;compound scaling 联合调节输入分辨率、深度、宽度。D0/D1 边缘可用,小目标比 YOLO 强,代价是延迟略高。
why_en: Two things: a BiFPN (bidirectional feature pyramid) fuses multi-scale features both ways so semantics and fine detail flow together, helping small objects, and compound scaling jointly tunes resolution, depth, and width; D0/D1 are edge-viable and beat YOLO on small objects at slightly higher latency.
options: 靠把 anchor 数量翻十倍来覆盖更多小框,所以小目标更准
靠纯注意力去掉 NMS,让重叠小目标不再互相压制
靠只保留最高分辨率一层特征图,牺牲大目标换小目标
靠 BiFPN 双向多尺度融合 + compound scaling 联合调分辨率/深度/宽度
options_en: By multiplying the number of anchors tenfold to cover more small boxes, so small objects get more accurate.
By using pure attention to drop NMS so overlapping small objects no longer suppress each other.
By keeping only the single highest-resolution feature map, trading big objects for small ones.
By a BiFPN for bidirectional multi-scale fusion plus compound scaling that jointly tunes resolution, depth, and width.
optionExplanations: 堆 anchor 只增计算不解决多尺度融合,EfficientDet 的小目标优势来自特征融合而非 anchor 数量。
去 NMS+纯注意力是 DETR 的做法,不是 EfficientDet。
只留一层反而丢掉多尺度信息,和 BiFPN 融合多尺度的思路正相反。
对;双向金字塔让细节与语义互相补,compound scaling 保证放大时三个维度协调,兼顾小目标与延迟。
optionExplanations_en: Piling on anchors only adds compute without solving multi-scale fusion; EfficientDet's small-object edge comes from feature fusion, not anchor count.
Dropping NMS with pure attention is DETR's approach, not EfficientDet's.
Keeping one layer throws away multi-scale information, the opposite of BiFPN's multi-scale fusion.
Correct — the bidirectional pyramid lets detail and semantics reinforce each other, and compound scaling keeps all three dimensions coordinated when scaling up.

termDefinitions.meaning: 一族用 BiFPN 和 compound scaling 的高效检测器,D0-D7 由小到大。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: EfficientDet is a family of efficient detectors using BiFPN and compound scaling, from small D0 to large D7.

termDefinitions.meaning: 双向特征金字塔:特征在自顶向下和自底向上两个方向融合,兼顾语义与细节。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: BiFPN (Bidirectional Feature Pyramid Network) fuses features in both top-down and bottom-up directions to combine semantics and detail.

termDefinitions.meaning: 同时按一组系数放大输入分辨率、网络深度和宽度,而不是只加深或只加宽。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Compound scaling jointly scales input resolution, depth, and width by a coordinated set of coefficients rather than one dimension alone.

q: 补全 EfficientDet 的两个核心组件：
q_en: Fill in EfficientDet's two core components:
text: EfficientDet 用 {{BiFPN}}(双向特征金字塔)做多尺度特征融合,再配合 {{compound scaling}} 联合调节输入分辨率、网络深度和宽度。
text_en: EfficientDet uses a {{BiFPN}} (bidirectional feature pyramid) for multi-scale fusion, plus {{compound scaling}} to jointly tune input resolution, depth, and width.
why: BiFPN 负责'把不同尺度特征融好'(利于小目标),compound scaling 负责'放大时三个维度一起动'(不失衡)。两者合起来让 EfficientDet 在中等延迟拿到强小目标检测。
why_en: BiFPN handles fusing multi-scale features for small objects, while compound scaling grows resolution, depth, and width together so scaling stays balanced.

termDefinitions.meaning: 双向特征金字塔,自顶向下+自底向上融合多尺度特征。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: BiFPN (Bidirectional Feature Pyramid Network) fuses multi-scale features both top-down and bottom-up.

termDefinitions.meaning: 按协调系数同时放大分辨率、深度、宽度。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Compound scaling scales resolution, depth, and width together by coordinated coefficients.

q: DETR 相比 YOLO/EfficientDet 在设计上最大的不同是什么？
q_en: What is DETR's biggest design difference from YOLO or EfficientDet?
why: DETR = Detection Transformer,用注意力把检测当集合预测,直接去掉了手工设计的 anchor 和 NMS 后处理,擅长处理大量重叠目标。代价是延迟高(Jetson 上约 85ms)、访存大,没有重度蒸馏基本不适合边缘。
why_en: DETR (Detection Transformer) frames detection as set prediction via attention, removing hand-designed anchors and NMS post-processing and handling many overlapping objects, but at high latency (around 85ms on Jetson) and memory, so it's unfit for the edge without heavy distillation.
options: 它是最轻量的单阶段 CNN,专为 sub-5ms 边缘推理设计
用注意力做集合预测,去掉手工 anchor 和 NMS,但延迟高、访存大,边缘需重度蒸馏
它靠增加 anchor 密度来提升召回,后处理反而更重
它只在 CPU 上跑,不需要 GPU,所以适合低功耗边缘设备
options_en: It is the lightest single-stage CNN, purpose-built for sub-5ms edge inference.
It does set prediction with attention, dropping hand-designed anchors and NMS, but at high latency and memory, needing heavy distillation for the edge.
It boosts recall by increasing anchor density, making post-processing heavier instead.
It runs on CPU only with no GPU needed, making it ideal for low-power edge devices.
optionExplanations: DETR 是三者里最重的,在 Jetson 上要跑 85ms 左右,和'最轻量 sub-5ms'的说法相反。
对;去 anchor 去 NMS 是它的卖点,但 Transformer 的延迟与访存让它在边缘水土不服。
它是去掉 anchor,不是增加 anchor;后处理也因为无 NMS 而更简洁。
Transformer 注意力在 CPU 上更慢,DETR 并非 CPU 友好,更谈不上低功耗。
optionExplanations_en: DETR is actually the heaviest of the three at around 85ms on Jetson, opposite to 'lightest sub-5ms'.
Correct — dropping anchors and NMS is its selling point, but Transformer latency and memory make it a poor edge fit.
It removes anchors rather than adding them, and post-processing is simpler because there is no NMS.
Transformer attention is even slower on CPU; DETR is not CPU-friendly, let alone low-power.

termDefinitions.meaning: 用 Transformer 注意力把目标检测当集合预测的模型,去掉 anchor 和 NMS。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: DETR (Detection Transformer) uses Transformer attention to treat detection as set prediction, removing anchors and NMS.

termDefinitions.meaning: 非极大值抑制:检测后处理,去掉互相重叠、指向同一目标的冗余框。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: NMS (Non-Maximum Suppression) is a post-processing step that removes redundant overlapping boxes pointing at the same object.

termDefinitions.meaning: 知识蒸馏:用大模型(teacher)指导小模型(student),把大模型能力压进小模型。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Distillation trains a small student model to mimic a large teacher, compressing the teacher's ability into the smaller model.

q: 在 Jetson AGX 上,YOLOv8-S、EfficientDet-D1、DETR 该怎么按延迟/mAP 权衡看？
q_en: On Jetson AGX, how do YOLOv8-S, EfficientDet-D1, and DETR compare on latency versus mAP?
why: 这是 mAP vs ms/帧 的约束优化,不是'谁最强'。YOLOv8-S 约 8ms/44.9% 最快、边缘首选;EfficientDet-D1 约 15ms/40.5% 但多尺度融合、小目标更好;DETR 约 85ms/42% 无 anchor/NMS 但边缘延迟难以接受。
why_en: It's a mAP-versus-ms/frame constrained optimization, not 'who's strongest': YOLOv8-S at ~8ms/44.9% is fastest and the edge default, EfficientDet-D1 at ~15ms/40.5% has better small-object fusion, and DETR at ~85ms/42% drops anchors/NMS but is too slow for the edge.
tradeoff: YOLO 的极致速度 vs EfficientDet 的小目标融合 vs DETR 的无锚无 NMS 但高延迟
options: YOLOv8-S 约 8ms 最快,EfficientDet-D1 约 15ms 小目标更好,DETR 约 85ms 边缘太慢
三者延迟其实差不多,选谁只看 mAP,DETR 的 42% 虽非最高但无 NMS 所以边缘首选
DETR 参数最省、跑得最快,YOLOv8-S 反而最慢,EfficientDet-D1 参数最多最重
参数越多延迟越低,所以 DETR 的 41M 参数让它在 Jetson 上比 YOLO 更快出结果
options_en: YOLOv8-S at ~8ms is fastest, EfficientDet-D1 at ~15ms is better on small objects, DETR at ~85ms is too slow for the edge.
Their latencies are actually about the same, so pick by mAP alone, and DETR's 42% though not highest is NMS-free so it's the edge default.
DETR is the most parameter-frugal and fastest, YOLOv8-S is the slowest, and EfficientDet-D1 is the heaviest with the most parameters.
More parameters means lower latency, so DETR's 41M parameters make it faster on Jetson than YOLO.
optionExplanations: 对;三者延迟差一个数量级(8 vs 15 vs 85ms),边缘首先按延迟预算筛,再在够快的里看 mAP 和小目标。
延迟根本不一样,DETR 85ms 已爆边缘预算,mAP 再高也用不上。
说反了:DETR 最慢、参数最多(41M),YOLO 才是最快那个。
参数多通常延迟更高而非更低,DETR 41M 正对应它 85ms 的高延迟。
optionExplanations_en: Correct — the latencies differ by an order of magnitude (8 vs 15 vs 85ms), so the edge filters by latency budget first, then compares mAP and small-object skill among the fast enough.
Latencies are not the same; DETR's 85ms already blows the edge budget, so higher mAP is unusable.

对;约束先行让你的取舍有锚点,每个架构的取用都能对着约束讲清楚。
不下结论等于没回答,系统设计要的是有理由的选择而非罗列。

q: 压缩流水线里,剪枝和量化的先后顺序为什么重要？
q_en: Why does the order of pruning and quantization matter in the compression pipeline?
why: 顺序是先剪枝再量化,因为两者的加速是乘性叠加:先剪掉 30-50% 通道把维度做小,再把剩下的权重从 FP32 降到 INT8,收益相乘。反过来先量化再剪,量化的定点表示会让通道重要性评估失真,剪得不准。
why_en: The order is prune then quantize because their speedups compound multiplicatively: first cut 30-50% of channels to shrink dimensions, then drop the remaining weights from FP32 to INT8, and the gains multiply, whereas quantizing first distorts the channel-importance estimate used by pruning.
diagram:
flowchart LR P["结构化剪枝
删 30-50% 通道"] --> F["微调恢复精度"] F --> Q["量化 FP32→INT8"] Q --> R["目标硬件重新 profile"]
options: 先剪枝再量化:两者加速乘性叠加,先缩小维度再降精度收益相乘
先量化再剪枝:定点权重更好评估通道重要性,剪得更准
顺序无所谓:剪枝和量化互不影响,并行做即可
只做其一即可:剪枝和量化本质等价,做两次是浪费
options_en: Prune then quantize — their speedups compound multiplicatively, shrinking dimensions before lowering precision.
Quantize then prune — fixed-point weights better estimate channel importance, so pruning is more accurate.
Order doesn't matter — pruning and quantization are independent, so do them in parallel.
Do only one — pruning and quantization are essentially equivalent, so doing both wastes effort.
optionExplanations: 对;剪枝把维度做小、量化把每个权重做小,先剪再量让两份收益相乘,这是标准管线。
量化后权重变定点,反而让基于 L1 范数的通道重要性失真,剪得更差不是更准。
两者都改权重与算子,量化会影响剪枝的重要性评估,并非互不影响。
剪枝减维度、量化降位宽,机制不同、收益叠加,不能相互替代。
optionExplanations_en: Correct — pruning shrinks dimensions and quantization shrinks each weight, so prune-then-quantize multiplies both gains, the standard pipeline.
Quantized fixed-point weights actually distort L1-norm channel importance, making pruning worse, not more accurate.
Both modify weights and operators, and quantization affects pruning's importance estimate, so they're not independent.
Pruning cuts dimensions while quantization cuts bit-width; different mechanisms whose gains stack, so they don't substitute.

termDefinitions.meaning: 删掉不重要的权重或通道来减小模型,结构化剪枝按通道整块删。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Pruning removes unimportant weights or channels to shrink a model; structured pruning removes whole channels.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把权重和激活的数值精度从高位降到低位(如 FP32→INT8)。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Quantization lowers the numeric precision of weights and activations, e.g. FP32 to INT8.

termDefinitions.meaning: 两步的加速比相乘而非相加,合起来收益更大。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Multiplicative means the two steps' speedup ratios multiply rather than add, giving a larger combined gain.

q: 把边缘检测模型的压缩流水线排成正确顺序：
q_en: Order the edge-detection compression pipeline correctly:
steps: 量化 FP32→INT8(选 PTQ 或 QAT)
结构化剪枝:按 L1 范数删掉最不重要的通道
在目标硬件上重新 profile,实测 wall-clock 延迟
剪枝后在原始数据上微调,恢复掉的精度
置信度校准(温度缩放),再接入 fail-safe
why: 先剪枝缩维度→微调把剪掉的精度救回来→再量化降位宽(乘性叠加)→到目标硬件实测延迟(FLOP 降不等于 wall-clock 降)→最后校准置信度接 fail-safe。跳过微调会带着掉的精度往下走,跳过重新 profile 会误信理论加速。
why_en: Prune to shrink dimensions, fine-tune to recover the lost accuracy, then quantize to cut bit-width (compounding), re-profile on the target hardware since FLOP cuts aren't wall-clock cuts, and finally calibrate confidence for fail-safe; skipping fine-tune carries lost accuracy forward and skipping re-profile trusts theoretical speedup.
diagram:
flowchart LR
  A["剪枝"] --> B["微调"]
  B --> C["量化"]
  C --> D["重新 profile"]
  D --> E["校准"]

termDefinitions.meaning: 真实设备上跑一遍的实际耗时,区别于理论 FLOP 数。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Wall-clock latency is the actual time a run takes on real hardware, as opposed to a theoretical FLOP count.

termDefinitions.meaning: 浮点运算次数,理论计算量指标,不直接等于实测延迟。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: FLOP (Floating Point Operations) counts arithmetic operations, a theoretical compute measure that doesn't equal measured latency.

termDefinitions.meaning: 训练后量化,用小校准集设定数值范围,快但可能伤尾类。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: PTQ (Post-Training Quantization) quantizes after training using a small calibration set, fast but can hurt rare classes.

q: 结构化剪枝具体删掉什么,又靠什么把精度救回来？
q_en: What does structured pruning remove, and how is accuracy recovered?
why: 结构化剪枝按 L1 范数(权重绝对值大小)找出最不重要的通道整块删掉,直接缩小层的维度。通常剪 30-50% 通道,删完精度会掉,再在原始数据上微调让剩余通道重新适应,把精度补回来。
why_en: Structured pruning uses L1-norm magnitude to find the least-important channels and removes them wholesale, shrinking layer dimensions, typically 30-50%; accuracy drops, so you fine-tune on the original data to let the remaining channels readapt and recover it.
options: 随机丢弃单个权重做稀疏化,靠更大的 batch 补回精度
删掉输出层的类别,靠减少类别数来提速
按 L1 范数删最不重要的整条通道(剪 30-50%),再在原始数据上微调恢复精度
删掉训练数据里的难样本,让模型只学简单样本来变快
options_en: Randomly drop individual weights for sparsity, and recover accuracy with a larger batch.
Delete classes from the output layer, speeding up by reducing the number of classes.
Remove the least-important whole channels by L1-norm (30-50%), then fine-tune on original data to recover.
Delete hard training samples so the model only learns easy ones and runs faster.
optionExplanations: 随机丢单权重是非结构化稀疏,不缩物理维度,边缘硬件难利用,也不是这里的做法。
删类别改变的是任务而非模型结构,不是剪枝。
对;整通道删才能真正缩层维、被硬件利用,微调是恢复精度的标准手段。
删难样本是改数据,和剪掉网络通道无关,还会伤泛化。
optionExplanations_en: Randomly dropping single weights is unstructured sparsity that doesn't shrink physical dimensions and is hard for edge hardware to exploit — not this.
Deleting classes changes the task, not the model structure, so it isn't pruning.
Correct — removing whole channels truly shrinks layer dimensions that hardware can exploit, and fine-tuning is the standard accuracy-recovery step.
Deleting hard samples changes the data, unrelated to removing network channels, and hurts generalization.

termDefinitions.meaning: 按通道/滤波器整块删除,真正缩小层维度,便于硬件加速。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Structured pruning removes whole channels or filters, genuinely shrinking layer dimensions so hardware can speed up.

termDefinitions.meaning: 权重绝对值之和,用作通道重要性的度量,越小越可删。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The L1-norm is the sum of absolute weight values, used as a channel-importance measure where smaller means more prunable.

termDefinitions.meaning: 剪枝后用原始数据继续训练几轮,让剩余通道适应、找回精度。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Fine-tuning trains a few more epochs on the original data after pruning so the remaining channels readapt and recover accuracy.

scenario: 剪枝后理论 FLOP 降了 40%,团队据此宣称推理会快 40%。
scenario_en: After pruning, theoretical FLOPs dropped 40%, and the team claims inference will get 40% faster.
q: 为什么必须在目标硬件上重新 profile,而不能只信 FLOP？
q_en: Why must you re-profile on target hardware instead of trusting FLOPs alone?
why: 因为剪枝物理删掉了计算单元,实测加速取决于剩下的维度是否对齐设备的访存/并行结构。40% 的 FLOP 削减可能只换来 25% 的 wall-clock 加速——如果剪后的通道数没对齐硬件的内存层级或 SIMD 宽度,算子反而利用率低。所以要在目标硬件实测。
why_en: Pruning physically removes compute units, so the real speedup depends on whether the leftover dimensions align with the device's memory and parallelism, and a 40% FLOP cut may yield only 25% wall-clock speedup when pruned channel counts misalign with the memory hierarchy or SIMD width, so you re-profile on the target hardware.
options: 不必重新 profile,FLOP 降多少延迟就降多少,40% 就是 40%
重新 profile 只是为了测功耗,和延迟无关
FLOP 越低模型越准,profile 是为了确认精度而非速度
剪枝物理删算子,若剪后维度不对齐访存/并行结构,40% FLOP 可能只换来约 25% 实测加速
options_en: No need to re-profile — latency drops exactly as FLOPs drop, so 40% means 40%.
Re-profiling only measures power draw and has nothing to do with latency.
Lower FLOPs means higher accuracy, so profiling confirms accuracy, not speed.
Pruning physically removes ops, and if leftover dimensions misalign with memory/parallelism, a 40% FLOP cut may yield only ~25% measured speedup.

termDefinitions.meaning: 浮点运算次数,理论计算量,不等于实测延迟。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: FLOP (Floating Point Operations) is a theoretical compute count that does not equal measured latency.

termDefinitions.meaning: 寄存器→缓存→显存的层级,维度不对齐会导致访存低效、算子跑不满。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The memory hierarchy spans registers, caches, and device memory; misaligned dimensions cause inefficient access and underutilized compute.

termDefinitions.meaning: 真实设备上跑一遍的实际耗时。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Wall-clock latency is the actual elapsed time of a run on real hardware.

optionExplanations: FLOP 和实测延迟不是线性对应,访存/并行结构是否对齐才决定实际能省多少。
profile 测的是真实耗时,不是功耗,这个说法把用途搞错了。
FLOP 衡量的是计算量而非精度,重新 profile 的目的是测速度,不是测准不准。
对;算子被物理删掉后,能省多少要看剩下的通道数合不合硬件的访存/并行结构,不能只信 FLOP。
optionExplanations_en: FLOPs and real latency aren't linearly tied — the actual speedup hinges on if the shrunk layout fits the chip's memory access and parallel execution patterns.
Profiling measures real elapsed time, not power draw — this mixes up what the re-profile step is even for.
FLOPs measure compute volume, not accuracy — the re-profile step checks speed, not correctness.
Correct — pruning cuts real hardware resources, so what you actually get back is set by whether the resulting layer widths fit the chip's memory access and parallel execution, not by FLOPs.

q: PTQ(训练后量化)怎么工作,它的主要风险是什么？
q_en: How does PTQ (post-training quantization) work, and what is its main risk?
why: PTQ 在训练完之后做:用一个小校准集跑几遍,统计激活/权重的数值范围,据此把 FP32 映射到 INT8,快且不用重训。风险是若校准集里稀有类样本太少,数值范围会为常见类优化,稀有类落到量化区间外→稀有类精度掉。
why_en: PTQ runs after training: a small calibration set is passed through to measure activation and weight value ranges, which map FP32 to INT8 quickly without retraining, but if the calibration set underrepresents rare classes the ranges optimize for common objects and rare-class accuracy degrades.
options: PTQ 在训练中插入伪量化节点让模型边训边补偿,所以最准
PTQ 训练后用小校准集设定数值范围映射 INT8,快但校准欠代表稀有类会伤稀有类精度
PTQ 需要完整重训一遍模型,是最慢的量化方式
PTQ 会自动扩大模型容量,量化后精度不降反升
options_en: PTQ inserts fake-quant nodes during training so the model compensates as it trains, making it the most accurate.
PTQ sets value ranges from a small post-training calibration set to map INT8 — fast, but underrepresenting rare classes hurts their accuracy.
PTQ requires fully retraining the model, making it the slowest quantization method.
PTQ automatically expands model capacity, so accuracy rises rather than falls after quantization.
optionExplanations: 训练中插伪量化节点是 QAT 的定义,不是 PTQ。
对;PTQ 的卖点是快、免重训,代价是校准集不均衡时数值范围偏向常见类,尾类吃亏。
PTQ 恰恰不用重训,这是它比 QAT 快的原因。
量化是降精度,只会掉或持平,不会自动增容涨精度。
optionExplanations_en: Inserting fake-quant nodes during training is the definition of QAT, not PTQ.
Correct — PTQ's selling point is speed with no retraining, at the cost that an unbalanced calibration set biases ranges toward common classes and hurts the tail.
PTQ specifically avoids retraining, which is why it's faster than QAT.
Quantization lowers precision and can only drop or hold accuracy, never auto-expand capacity to raise it.

termDefinitions.meaning: 训练后量化:用小校准集统计数值范围,把 FP32 映射到 INT8,无需重训。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: PTQ (Post-Training Quantization) uses a small calibration set to measure value ranges and map FP32 to INT8 without retraining.

termDefinitions.meaning: 一小批代表性数据,用来统计激活范围以设定量化刻度。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A calibration set is a small representative batch used to measure activation ranges and set quantization scales.

termDefinitions.meaning: FP32 是 32 位浮点,INT8 是 8 位整数,量化把前者压成后者。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: FP32 is 32-bit floating point and INT8 is 8-bit integer; quantization compresses the former into the latter.

q: QAT(量化感知训练)靠什么把量化后的精度损失压到很小？
q_en: How does QAT (quantization-aware training) keep post-quantization accuracy loss tiny?
why: QAT 在训练的前向传播里插入伪量化节点(fake quantization),让模型在训练时就'看到'量化误差,反向传播时学着补偿它。这样部署到 INT8 边缘加速器上时,精度通常还在全精度的 1% mAP 以内,代价是要重新训练。
why_en: QAT inserts fake-quantization nodes into the training forward pass so the model sees quantization error during training and learns to compensate via backprop, so on INT8 edge accelerators it typically stays within 1% mAP of full precision, at the cost of retraining.
options: 训练后再用一个大校准集统计数值范围来映射,完全不改训练过程
把所有权重四舍五入成整数后直接冻结,不再做任何训练或补偿
在训练前向里插伪量化节点,让模型学着补偿量化误差,部署后常在全精度 1% mAP 内
只量化网络最后一层,前面各层全保持 FP32,所以几乎不掉精度
options_en: It measures value ranges with a large calibration set after training and maps them, without changing the training process at all.
It rounds all weights to integers and freezes them directly, doing no further training or compensation.
It inserts fake-quant nodes into the training forward pass so the model learns to compensate, staying within ~1% mAP of full precision.
It quantizes only the network's last layer and keeps every earlier layer FP32, so accuracy barely drops.
optionExplanations: 训练后统计范围、不改训练是 PTQ 的做法,不是 QAT。
冻结成整数不训练就无从补偿量化误差,和 QAT 的核心机制相反。
对;伪量化节点让模型在训练时把量化误差当成一部分学进去,所以部署后损失很小。
只量化一层既省不了多少,也不是 QAT 的机制,QAT 是全模型感知量化训练。
optionExplanations_en: Measuring ranges after training without changing training is PTQ's approach, not QAT's.
Freezing to integers without training gives no way to compensate quantization error, the opposite of QAT's core mechanism.
Correct — fake-quant nodes let the model learn quantization error as part of training, so deployment loss is small.
Quantizing one layer saves little and isn't QAT's mechanism; QAT trains the whole model quantization-aware.

termDefinitions.meaning: 量化感知训练:训练时插伪量化节点,让模型学着补偿量化误差。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: QAT (Quantization-Aware Training) inserts fake-quant nodes during training so the model learns to compensate for quantization error.

termDefinitions.meaning: 前向里模拟量化-反量化的算子,让梯度能感知量化误差。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Fake quantization simulates quantize-dequantize in the forward pass so gradients can perceive quantization error.

termDefinitions.meaning: 车载/嵌入式上专跑 INT8 推理的加速芯片。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An edge accelerator is an on-board or embedded chip specialized for INT8 inference.

q: PTQ 和 QAT 在成本、精度、是否重训上怎么权衡？
q_en: How do PTQ and QAT trade off on cost, accuracy, and retraining?
why: PTQ 快、免重训,只要小校准集,但校准欠代表时尾类精度掉得多;QAT 要重新训练、插伪量化节点,慢且贵,换来通常在全精度 1% mAP 内的精度。选择轴是'速度/成本 vs 精度尤其尾类精度'。
why_en: PTQ is fast and retraining-free with just a small calibration set but can lose tail-class accuracy when calibration is unbalanced, while QAT retrains with fake-quant nodes — slower and costlier — but usually lands within 1% mAP of full precision, so the axis is speed/cost versus accuracy, especially on the tail.
tradeoff: PTQ 的快与免重训 vs QAT 的高精度但需重训
options: PTQ 更准更慢,QAT 更快更省,应总是优先 PTQ
两者都需重训,区别只在校准集大小
PTQ 无差别地伤所有类别,QAT 无差别地保所有类别
PTQ 快、免重训但校准不均易伤尾类;QAT 需重训但精度常在全精度 1% mAP 内
options_en: PTQ is more accurate and slower, QAT is faster and cheaper, so always prefer PTQ.
Both require retraining, and the only difference is calibration-set size.
PTQ hurts all classes uniformly and QAT preserves all classes uniformly.
PTQ is fast and retraining-free but unbalanced calibration hurts the tail; QAT needs retraining but usually stays within 1% mAP of full precision.
optionExplanations: 说反了:PTQ 更快、QAT 更准,而且哪个'优先'取决于精度要求,不是无脑选 PTQ。
PTQ 恰恰不需重训,这是它比 QAT 快的根本原因。
PTQ 对尾类伤害更大(不是均匀),QAT 也非绝对无损,只是常在 1% 内。
对;这条准确点出速度/成本与精度尤其尾类精度这条取舍轴。
optionExplanations_en: Reversed — PTQ is faster and QAT is more accurate, and which to prefer depends on accuracy needs, not defaulting to PTQ.
PTQ specifically needs no retraining, the very reason it's faster than QAT.
PTQ hurts the tail disproportionately, not uniformly, and QAT isn't lossless, just usually within 1%.
Correct — this pins the speed/cost versus accuracy (especially tail) axis precisely.

termDefinitions.meaning: 训练后量化,快、免重训,校准不均时伤尾类。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: PTQ (Post-Training Quantization) is fast and retraining-free but hurts tail classes under unbalanced calibration.

termDefinitions.meaning: 量化感知训练,需重训,精度常在全精度 1% mAP 内。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: QAT (Quantization-Aware Training) retrains the model and usually stays within 1% mAP of full precision.

termDefinitions.meaning: 样本稀少的稀有类别,压缩时最容易被牺牲。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A tail class is a rare, low-sample category most easily sacrificed during compression.

scenario: 一个检测器压缩后,汽车类 mAP 只掉 0.5%,团队据此宣布压缩无损,但轮椅类 mAP 掉了 8%。
scenario_en: After compression a detector loses only 0.5% mAP on cars, and the team declares it lossless, but the wheelchair class drops 8% mAP.
q: 激进压缩为什么会不成比例地伤害稀有类,这有什么安全含义？
q_en: Why does aggressive compression disproportionately hurt rare classes, and what's the safety implication?
why: 这是长尾分布问题:常见类(汽车)样本多、特征冗余,剪枝/量化误差被平均掉;稀有类(轮椅)样本少、表征脆弱,一压就崩。只看整体或常见类 mAP 会掩盖 8% 的尾类塌陷,而轮椅正是安全攸关目标,所以必须按类别分层评估。
why_en: It's the long-tail problem: common classes like cars have abundant redundant features so pruning/quantization error averages out, while rare classes like wheelchairs have few samples and fragile representations that collapse under compression, and aggregate or common-class mAP hides the 8% tail drop even though wheelchairs are safety-critical, so evaluate per class.
options: 长尾问题:稀有类样本少、表征脆弱,一压就崩;整体 mAP 会掩盖尾类塌陷,必须按类别评估
稀有类天生比常见类更鲁棒,8% 只是测量噪声,可忽略
只要整体 mAP 掉得少就算无损,单个类别的下降不重要
稀有类掉分是因为它们本来就不该被检测,压缩帮忙过滤掉了它们
options_en: Long-tail problem: rare classes have few samples and fragile representations that collapse under compression, and aggregate mAP hides the tail drop, so evaluate per class.
Rare classes are inherently more robust than common ones, so the 8% is just measurement noise and can be ignored.
As long as aggregate mAP drops little it's lossless, and individual class drops don't matter.
Rare classes lose accuracy because they shouldn't be detected anyway, and compression helpfully filters them out.

termDefinitions.meaning: 少数常见类占绝大多数样本,大量稀有类各自样本极少。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A long-tail distribution has a few common classes dominating samples and many rare classes each with very few.

termDefinitions.meaning: 对每个类别单独算 mAP,能暴露被整体平均掩盖的尾类塌陷。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Per-class mAP computes the metric for each class separately, exposing tail collapse that aggregate averaging hides.

optionExplanations: 对;常见类样本多能扛住压缩误差,稀有类样本少一压就崩,只看整体分数会把这 8% 藏起来。
8% 是能稳定复现的下降,不是噪声,而且稀有类恰恰因为样本少更脆弱,不是更鲁棒。
轮椅这类目标是安全攸关的,单类别塌陷不能被'整体没大掉'这句话糊弄过去。
压缩不会替你'过滤该检测的目标',轮椅仍是要被识别的安全目标,这个说法倒因为果。
optionExplanations_en: Correct — classes with lots of examples can absorb compression error better, while ones with few examples fall apart, and the aggregate score hides that 8% collapse.
An 8% drop that repeats isn't noise, and low-sample classes are more fragile because they have so few examples, not more robust.
A collapse this size on a single safety-relevant class can't be waved away just because the overall number barely moved.
Compression doesn't 'helpfully filter' targets — wheelchairs still need to be detected, so this gets cause and effect backwards.

scenario: 一条示例压缩流水线把 YOLOv8 从 100MB 压到 14MB。
scenario_en: An example compression pipeline shrinks YOLOv8 from 100MB to 14MB.
q: 100MB→14MB 这个约 7 倍压缩对边缘部署意味着什么？
q_en: What does the 100MB-to-14MB (~7x) compression mean for edge deployment?
why: 约 7 倍压缩(100/14 ≈ 7)来自剪枝+量化的乘性叠加,不是单一公式。下游用途:更小的模型能装进车载有限的存储和显存、加载更快、访存带宽压力更低,这才是它能在 Jetson 实时跑的前提;但要同时核对压缩后 mAP 尤其尾类没崩。
why_en: The ~7x (100/14) comes from pruning plus quantization compounding, not a single formula, and downstream it lets the model fit the car's limited storage and device memory, load faster, and ease memory-bandwidth pressure — the precondition for real-time Jetson inference — provided you verify post-compression mAP, especially the tail, hasn't collapsed.
options: 14MB 只是磁盘占用,和推理速度、显存无关,纯粹是省硬盘
约 7 倍压缩让模型装进车载有限存储/显存、加载更快、访存压力更小,是边缘实时的前提
压到 14MB 一定无损,体积和精度无关,不用再验 mAP
越小越好,应继续压到 1MB,精度可以随便牺牲
options_en: 14MB is only disk footprint, unrelated to inference speed or device memory — purely saving disk.
The ~7x compression fits the model into the car's limited storage/memory, loads faster, and eases bandwidth — the precondition for edge real-time.
Compressing to 14MB is surely lossless; size and accuracy are unrelated, so no need to re-check mAP.
Smaller is always better, so keep compressing to 1MB and sacrifice accuracy freely.

termDefinitions.meaning: 权重占用的字节数,影响存储、加载和访存带宽,间接影响延迟。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Model size is the bytes the weights occupy, affecting storage, load time, and memory bandwidth, and thus latency.

termDefinitions.meaning: 边缘 GPU 上的有限内存,模型和中间激活都要放得下。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Device memory is the limited memory on an edge GPU that must hold the model and intermediate activations.

optionExplanations: 模型体积同样占用显存和访存带宽,不是只关磁盘,这个说法漏掉了推理侧的影响。
对;只有把模型压小,才挤得进车载那点存储和显存,这才是能在 Jetson 上实时跑起来的先决条件。
体积变小不保证精度没掉,尾类恰恰最容易在压缩里被牺牲,还是得重新核对 mAP。
体积不是压得越小越好,精度尤其安全攸关目标的精度是硬约束,不能随便牺牲。
optionExplanations_en: Model size also affects how much of the chip's memory and bandwidth it needs, not just the disk footprint — this misses the inference-side impact entirely.
Correct — shrinking the model is what lets it squeeze into the car's tight storage and memory with faster loads, the very thing that makes running real-time on Jetson possible.
Smaller size doesn't guarantee accuracy holds — the tail is exactly what tends to collapse under compression, so mAP still needs rechecking.
Smaller isn't automatically better — accuracy, especially for safety-critical classes, is a hard constraint you can't trade away freely.

scenario: 对 YOLOv8 做了 40% 剪枝 + PTQ,常见类 mAP 稳定,但轮椅、婴儿车这类稀有类 mAP 掉了 8%。
scenario_en: You apply 40% pruning + PTQ to YOLOv8; common-class mAP is stable but rare classes like wheelchairs and strollers drop 8% mAP.
q: 最可能的根因和修法是什么？
q_en: What is the most likely root cause and fix?
why: 根因是 PTQ 的校准集欠代表稀有类:量化数值范围为常见类优化,稀有类激活落到范围外被截断→尾类精度崩。修法是改用 QAT 并配一个类别更均衡的校准集,让模型在训练时就补偿量化误差、覆盖尾类。
why_en: The root cause is that PTQ's calibration set underrepresents rare classes, so the quantization ranges optimize for common objects and rare-class activations get clipped, collapsing the tail; the fix is QAT with a class-balanced calibration set so the model compensates for quantization error and covers the tail during training.
tradeoff: PTQ 快但尾类脆 vs QAT+均衡校准慢但保尾类
whenOtherWins: 若尾类本就不在安全攸关范围、且要极快出边缘版本,保留 PTQ、只补稀有类校准样本可能就够。
options: 剪枝剪太狠,把稀有类的通道删光了,应该完全不剪枝
常见类过拟合,应删掉常见类训练数据重训
PTQ 校准集欠代表稀有类致尾类被截断;改用 QAT + 类别均衡校准集
这是正常现象,稀有类不重要,直接上线即可
options_en: Pruning was too aggressive and deleted all rare-class channels, so skip pruning entirely.
Common classes overfit, so delete common-class training data and retrain.
PTQ calibration underrepresents rare classes and clips the tail; switch to QAT with a class-balanced calibration set.
This is normal, rare classes don't matter, so just ship it.
optionExplanations: 现象是常见类稳、只有尾类掉,若是剪枝剪光稀有通道常见类也会受影响,根因指向量化校准而非全盘弃剪。
删常见类数据会两头受伤,且不解决量化范围偏差,方向错。
对;常见类稳、尾类崩正是 PTQ 校准偏向常见类的典型指纹,QAT+均衡校准是标准修法。
轮椅/婴儿车正是安全攸关目标,8% 尾类塌陷绝不能直接上线。
optionExplanations_en: Only the tail drops while common classes hold; if pruning had wiped rare channels, common classes would suffer too, so the cause points to quantization calibration, not abandoning pruning.
Deleting common-class data hurts both ends and doesn't fix the quantization-range bias — wrong direction.
Correct — stable common classes with a collapsed tail is the classic fingerprint of PTQ calibration biased to common objects, and QAT with balanced calibration is the standard fix.
Wheelchairs and strollers are exactly safety-critical targets, so an 8% tail collapse must never ship as-is.

termDefinitions.meaning: 训练后量化,靠校准集设范围,校准偏则尾类被截断。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: PTQ (Post-Training Quantization) sets ranges from a calibration set; a biased set clips tail-class activations.

termDefinitions.meaning: 量化感知训练,训练中补偿量化误差,保尾类更好。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: QAT (Quantization-Aware Training) compensates for quantization error during training and preserves the tail better.

termDefinitions.term: balanced calibration set / 均衡校准集
termDefinitions.meaning: 让稀有类在校准数据里有足够代表,避免数值范围只偏向常见类。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A balanced calibration set gives rare classes enough representation so ranges don't skew to common objects.

q: 补全量化把数值精度从哪降到哪：
q_en: Fill in what quantization lowers the numeric precision from and to:
text: 量化把权重与激活从 {{FP32}}(32 位浮点)降到 {{INT8}}(8 位整数),模型体积和访存带宽都随之下降,推理更快。
text_en: Quantization drops weights and activations from {{FP32}} (32-bit float) to {{INT8}} (8-bit integer), cutting both model size and memory bandwidth for faster inference.
why: 从 32 位降到 8 位,单个数值占用少 4 倍,体积和访存带宽同步下降,边缘加速器上 INT8 算子还有专门硬件支持,所以更快。代价是精度可能掉,尤其尾类。
why_en: Going from 32 bits to 8 bits makes each value 4x smaller, cutting size and bandwidth, and INT8 has dedicated hardware on edge accelerators, so it runs faster at the cost of some accuracy, especially on the tail.

termDefinitions.meaning: 32 位浮点,训练时的默认高精度数值格式。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: FP32 (32-bit Floating Point) is the default high-precision numeric format used in training.

termDefinitions.meaning: 8 位整数,量化目标格式,体积为 FP32 的四分之一。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: INT8 (8-bit Integer) is the quantization target format, a quarter the size of FP32.

q: 硬件感知 NAS 相比人手工在 YOLO 和 EfficientDet 里二选一,本质区别是什么？
q_en: What fundamentally distinguishes hardware-aware NAS from a human picking between YOLO and EfficientDet?
why: 硬件感知 NAS 用搜索算法自动评估成千上万个候选架构,而且是直接对着真实目标硬件的延迟来评,不是人凭经验在两三个现成架构里挑。它把架构设计变成一个多目标搜索:在真实设备约束下同时优化延迟和 mAP。
why_en: Hardware-aware NAS uses a search algorithm to automatically evaluate thousands of candidate architectures against the actual target hardware's measured latency, rather than a human choosing among two or three off-the-shelf designs by intuition, turning architecture design into a multi-objective search under real-device constraints.
options: NAS 只是把 YOLO 和 EfficientDet 拼在一起跑集成,不搜新架构
NAS 就是人手工调超参,只是换了个名字
NAS 只在云端用理论 FLOP 评估,从不接触真实硬件延迟
NAS 用搜索算法自动评估上千候选架构,直接对着真实目标硬件延迟来选
options_en: NAS just ensembles YOLO and EfficientDet together without searching new architectures.
NAS is manual hyperparameter tuning under a different name.
NAS only evaluates by theoretical FLOPs in the cloud and never touches real hardware latency.
NAS uses a search algorithm to automatically evaluate thousands of candidates against the actual target hardware's latency.
optionExplanations: NAS 是搜索全新结构,不是把两个现成模型做集成。
NAS 搜的是网络结构(层类型、通道、kernel),比手调超参的空间大得多,也自动得多。
'硬件感知'的关键正是接触真实硬件延迟(直接测或查延迟表),不是只看 FLOP。
对;自动搜大量候选 + 用真实硬件延迟当评判,是硬件感知 NAS 的定义。
optionExplanations_en: NAS searches genuinely new structures, not an ensemble of two existing models.
NAS searches network structure (layer types, channels, kernels), a far larger and more automated space than manual hyperparameter tuning.
The whole point of 'hardware-aware' is touching real hardware latency (measured or via a latency table), not just FLOPs.
Correct — automatically searching many candidates and judging by real hardware latency is the definition of hardware-aware NAS.

termDefinitions.meaning: 神经架构搜索:自动搜索网络结构,而非人工设计。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: NAS (Neural Architecture Search) automatically searches network structures instead of hand-designing them.

termDefinitions.meaning: 搜索时把真实目标硬件的延迟纳入评判,而非只看理论计算量。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Hardware-aware means the search judges candidates by the real target hardware's latency, not just theoretical compute.

q: 硬件感知 NAS 的搜索空间(building blocks)通常包含哪些？(多选)
q_en: What does a hardware-aware NAS search space (building blocks) typically include? (multiple)
why: 搜索空间是可组合的结构积木:各层的 kernel 尺寸、通道数、层类型,覆盖 backbone/neck/head 三段。控制器就是在这些积木的组合里采样候选架构。标注人力预算不是架构积木,属于数据侧,不在搜索空间里。
why_en: The search space is composable structural building blocks — per-layer kernel sizes, channel counts, and layer types across backbone, neck, and head — from which the controller samples candidate architectures; labeling budget is data-side, not an architectural block.
options: 各层的 kernel 尺寸
各层的通道数
backbone/neck/head 各段的层类型
标注团队的人力预算
options_en: Per-layer kernel sizes.
Per-layer channel counts.
Layer types across the backbone, neck, and head.
The labeling team's headcount budget.
optionExplanations: 对;kernel 尺寸是最基本的结构积木,直接影响感受野和计算量。
对;通道数决定每层宽度,是延迟和容量的主要旋钮。
对;backbone/neck/head 各段可选不同层类型,是检测器结构的三大部件。
错;人力预算是项目资源,不是网络结构积木,不属于 NAS 搜索空间。
optionExplanations_en: Correct — kernel size is a basic structural block that directly affects receptive field and compute.
Correct — channel count sets each layer's width, a main knob for latency and capacity.
Correct — backbone, neck, and head can each take different layer types, the three parts of a detector.
Incorrect — headcount is a project resource, not a network building block, so it isn't in the search space.

termDefinitions.meaning: 所有可被组合成候选架构的结构积木集合。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The search space is the set of structural building blocks that can be combined into candidate architectures.

termDefinitions.meaning: 检测器中连接 backbone 与 head、做多尺度特征融合的中段(如 FPN)。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The neck is the mid-section between backbone and head that fuses multi-scale features, such as an FPN.

termDefinitions.meaning: 检测器输出框和类别的最后部件。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The head is the detector's final part that outputs boxes and class labels.

q: NAS 控制器怎么评估一个候选架构的延迟,优化目标又是什么？
q_en: How does the NAS controller evaluate a candidate's latency, and what is it optimizing?
why: 控制器(RL agent 或进化算法)采样候选后,要么把它直接部署到目标设备实测延迟,要么查一个延迟查找表——该表按硬件的计算单元数和访存带宽标定过。目标是多目标:同时最小化延迟、最大化 mAP,而不是只追一个。
why_en: The controller (an RL agent or evolutionary algorithm) samples a candidate and either profiles it directly on the target device or queries a latency lookup table calibrated to the hardware's compute units and memory bandwidth, optimizing a multi-objective goal: minimize latency and maximize mAP together.
options: 只用参数量粗估延迟(参数越多算越低),优化目标是把候选的参数量最大化
控制器采样候选,直接在设备实测或查延迟查找表(按算力+访存带宽标定),多目标同时优化延迟与 mAP
对每个候选随机猜一个延迟值,只优化 mAP,延迟根本不进目标函数
把每个候选都训练到收敛再逐一比 mAP,完全不测也不估延迟
options_en: Estimate latency roughly from parameter count alone (more parameters means lower compute) and make the objective maximize a candidate's parameters.
The controller samples a candidate, profiles it on-device or via a latency lookup table (calibrated to compute + bandwidth), and multi-objective-optimizes latency and mAP.
Guess a random latency value for each candidate, optimize only mAP, and keep latency entirely out of the objective.
Train every candidate to convergence and compare mAP one by one, never measuring or estimating latency at all.
optionExplanations: 参数量既不能准确估延迟,更不是'越多越低',优化目标也不是最大化参数。
对;实测或查标定过的延迟表让延迟成为可优化信号,多目标才能兼顾快与准。
硬件感知 NAS 的核心就是把延迟纳入目标,随机猜、只优化 mAP 与它的定义相悖。
只比 mAP 不看延迟会搜出跑不动的架构,违背硬件感知的初衷。
optionExplanations_en: Parameter count neither estimates latency accurately nor means 'more is lower', and the objective isn't to maximize parameters.
Correct — measuring or querying a calibrated latency table makes latency an optimizable signal so the multi-objective balances fast and accurate.
Hardware-aware NAS's core is putting latency in the objective, so guessing and optimizing only mAP contradicts it.
Comparing mAP alone searches architectures that can't run, defeating the hardware-aware purpose.

termDefinitions.meaning: NAS 里采样候选架构的智能体,常是 RL agent 或进化算法。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The controller is the NAS agent that samples candidate architectures, often an RL agent or evolutionary algorithm.

termDefinitions.term: latency lookup table / 延迟查找表
termDefinitions.meaning: 预先按硬件算力和访存带宽标定的表,快速估候选延迟,免去每个都上机实测。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A latency lookup table is precalibrated to hardware compute and bandwidth to quickly estimate a candidate's latency without profiling each on-device.

termDefinitions.meaning: 同时优化两个或以上目标(此处延迟与 mAP),在其间找权衡。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Multi-objective optimization jointly optimizes two or more goals, here latency and mAP, trading them off.

scenario: 硬件感知 NAS 一次搜索要烧数千 GPU-hours,团队在纠结值不值得为车载检测器搞一次 NAS。
scenario_en: A hardware-aware NAS run burns thousands of GPU-hours, and the team debates whether it's worth doing for the on-board detector.
q: 什么时候 NAS 的高成本才划算？
q_en: When does NAS's high cost actually pay off?
why: NAS 值不值看规模:一次搜索烧数千 GPU-hours,只有在车队级(fleet scale)部署时才摊得平——每帧省 1ms,乘以每天数百万次调用,累积的算力/能耗节省巨大。小规模一次性项目直接选现成 YOLO/EfficientDet 更划算。
why_en: NAS's worth scales with deployment: a run costs thousands of GPU-hours and only amortizes at fleet scale, where shaving 1ms per frame across millions of daily calls yields huge cumulative compute and energy savings, whereas a small one-off project is better served by an off-the-shelf YOLO or EfficientDet.
tradeoff: NAS 数千 GPU-hours 的一次性成本 vs 车队级每毫秒的持续节省
whenOtherWins: 若只是单机原型或小批部署,现成架构 + 压缩就够,NAS 的一次性成本摊不平。
options: 车队级部署:每帧省 1ms × 每天数百万次调用,累积节省远超一次搜索的成本
任何项目都该先做 NAS,反正搜出来的架构一定最好
只有单机原型验证时才值,规模越小 NAS 越划算
NAS 能替代压缩,搜完就不用剪枝量化,所以总是省钱
options_en: Fleet-scale deployment: 1ms saved per frame times millions of daily calls yields cumulative savings far above one search's cost.
Every project should run NAS first, since the searched architecture is always best anyway.
It's only worth it for single-machine prototyping — the smaller the scale, the more NAS pays off.
NAS replaces compression, so after searching you skip pruning and quantization, making it always cheaper.
optionExplanations: 对;数千 GPU-hours 是固定投入,只有海量调用把每毫秒节省乘大,才摊得平这笔一次性成本。
小项目里 NAS 成本摊不平,盲目先搜是浪费,'一定最好'也不成立。
说反了:规模越小越不值,单机原型用现成架构即可。
NAS 不替代压缩,搜出的架构仍要剪枝+量化,这条前提就错。
optionExplanations_en: Correct — thousands of GPU-hours is a fixed cost that only amortizes when massive call volume multiplies the per-ms savings.
On small projects NAS cost never amortizes, so searching blindly wastes money, and 'always best' is false.
Reversed — smaller scale is less worth it, and a single-machine prototype should use an off-the-shelf architecture.
NAS doesn't replace compression; the searched architecture still gets pruned and quantized, so the premise is wrong.

termDefinitions.meaning: GPU 运行小时数,衡量搜索/训练的算力开销,数千即成本高昂。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: GPU-hours measure compute cost as GPUs multiplied by runtime; thousands means an expensive run.

termDefinitions.meaning: 同一模型部署到海量设备(整支车队),每点小优化被巨量调用放大。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Fleet scale means one model deployed across a huge device fleet, so each small optimization is amplified by enormous call volume.

scenario: 团队用 NAS 搜出了一个针对 Jetson 优化的检测架构,有人主张既然是硬件感知搜出来的,就不用再压缩了。
scenario_en: The team NAS-searched a Jetson-optimized detector, and someone argues that since it's hardware-aware-searched, no further compression is needed.
q: NAS 搜出的架构还要不要做剪枝和量化？
q_en: Does a NAS-searched architecture still need pruning and quantization?
why: 还要:NAS 解决的是'选/搜出一个好结构',压缩解决的是'把给定结构再做小做快',两者正交、可叠加。搜出的架构仍能通过剪掉冗余通道、量化到 INT8 进一步降延迟降体积,所以 NAS 不替代压缩,是压缩的上游。
why_en: Yes — NAS finds a good structure while compression shrinks and speeds up a given structure, so they're orthogonal and stack: the searched architecture can still drop redundant channels and quantize to INT8 for further latency and size cuts, so NAS is upstream of compression, not a replacement.
options: 不用了,NAS 已经硬件感知优化过,再压缩会破坏搜出的结构
不用了,NAS 和压缩是二选一的替代关系
还要:NAS 负责搜结构,压缩负责把结构再做小做快,两者正交可叠加
还要,但要先量化再 NAS,顺序反过来才对
options_en: No — NAS already optimized hardware-aware, and compressing would break the searched structure.
No — NAS and compression are mutually exclusive alternatives.
Yes — NAS finds the structure and compression shrinks and speeds it further; they're orthogonal and stack.
Yes, but quantize first then NAS — the order should be reversed.
optionExplanations: 压缩(尤其后接微调/QAT)不会破坏结构,反而在搜出的结构上继续挤延迟,'不用压'是误解。
两者目标不同、可叠加,不是替代;把它们对立起来会丢掉一层收益。
对;NAS 是上游选结构,压缩是下游榨性能,叠起来延迟和体积都能再降。
顺序反了:先有结构(NAS)才谈压缩,量化是压缩流水线里靠后的一步。
optionExplanations_en: Compression (especially with fine-tune/QAT after) doesn't break the structure but squeezes more latency out of it, so 'no compression' is a misconception.
They have different goals and stack rather than substitute; opposing them forfeits a layer of gains.
Correct — NAS is upstream structure selection and compression is downstream performance squeezing, stacking to cut latency and size further.
The order is backwards: you need a structure (NAS) before compressing, and quantization is a later step in the compression pipeline.

termDefinitions.meaning: 两种手段解决不同问题、互不冲突,可叠加使用。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Orthogonal means two techniques address different problems without conflict and can be combined.

termDefinitions.meaning: 自动搜网络结构,是压缩的上游,不替代压缩。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: NAS (Neural Architecture Search) automatically searches structures upstream of compression and does not replace it.

q: 把硬件感知 NAS 的搜索循环排成正确顺序：
q_en: Order the hardware-aware NAS search loop correctly:
steps: 控制器(RL agent / 进化算法)采样一个候选架构
多目标打分:最小化延迟 + 最大化 mAP
定义搜索空间:backbone/neck/head 的 kernel 尺寸、通道数、层类型
用得分更新控制器,采样下一个候选
在设备上或延迟查找表 profile 该候选的延迟
why: 先定义搜索空间(积木)→控制器采样一个候选→在真实设备或延迟表上 profile 它的延迟→用延迟+mAP 做多目标打分→用得分更新控制器,再采下一个,循环往复。跳过 profile 就失去硬件感知,退化成普通 NAS。
why_en: Define the search space of building blocks, have the controller sample a candidate, profile its latency on-device or via a table, score it multi-objective on latency and mAP, then update the controller and sample the next, looping on; skip profiling and you lose the hardware-awareness and degrade to plain NAS.
diagram:
flowchart LR
  S["定义搜索空间"] --> C["采样候选"]
  C --> P["profile 延迟"]
  P --> Sc["多目标打分"]
  Sc --> U["更新控制器"]
  U --> C

termDefinitions.meaning: 可组合成候选架构的结构积木集合,循环第一步先定义好。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The search space is the set of building blocks combined into candidates, defined first in the loop.

termDefinitions.meaning: 采样候选并按得分更新的智能体(RL 或进化算法)。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The controller samples candidates and updates itself by their scores, using RL or evolution.

scenario: 压缩后的检测器给一辆并不存在的车打 0.95 置信度(触发幽灵刹车),又给一个真实行人只打 0.3(被当噪声忽略)。
scenario_en: A compressed detector gives 0.95 confidence to a nonexistent car (triggering phantom braking) and only 0.3 to a real pedestrian (ignored as noise).
q: 这两个现象说明什么问题,为什么直接在 0.5 卡阈值是危险信号？
q_en: What do these two symptoms reveal, and why is thresholding at 0.5 a red flag?
why: 说明检测器置信度没校准:分数不再等于真实正确概率,高分误报(幽灵刹车)和低分漏真(忽略行人)同时出现。此时用固定 0.5 卡阈值会同时放过危险误报和真行人,因为 0.5 这个数在未校准的分数上没有一致含义。得先做校准让分数可信。
why_en: It shows the detector's confidence is uncalibrated: scores no longer equal true correctness probability, so high-score false positives (phantom braking) and low-score true misses (ignored pedestrian) coexist, and a fixed 0.5 threshold is meaningless on uncalibrated scores, so calibrate first to make scores trustworthy.
diagram:
flowchart TB U["未校准分数"] --> A["0.95 误报
幽灵刹车"] U --> B["0.3 真行人
被忽略"] A --> R["0.5 阈值不可信"] B --> R
options: 说明模型准确率太低,只要重训到更高 mAP,阈值问题自然消失
置信度未校准:分数不等于真实正确概率,0.5 阈值无一致含义,须先校准
说明该把阈值从 0.5 调到 0.95,把所有低分预测都当噪声丢掉
这是正常的,检测器分数本来就不用等于概率,忽略即可
options_en: It means accuracy is too low; just retrain to higher mAP and the threshold problem vanishes.
Confidence is uncalibrated: scores don't equal true correctness probability, so a 0.5 threshold has no consistent meaning and you must calibrate first.
It means raise the threshold from 0.5 to 0.95 and discard all low-score predictions as noise.
This is normal — detector scores were never meant to equal probability, so just ignore it.
optionExplanations: 更高 mAP 不保证分数校准,一个准的模型仍可能过度自信,阈值问题依旧。
对;核心是分数与真实概率脱钩,先校准再谈阈值,否则任何固定阈值都不可信。
调到 0.95 会漏掉那个只有 0.3 的真行人,反而更危险,不是修法。
在安全攸关系统里,分数必须可信到能支撑 fail-safe,'忽略即可'不可接受。
optionExplanations_en: Higher mAP doesn't guarantee calibrated scores; an accurate model can still be overconfident, so the threshold problem persists.
Correct — the core issue is scores decoupled from true probability, so calibrate before thresholding or any fixed cutoff is untrustworthy.
Raising to 0.95 drops the real pedestrian at 0.3, which is more dangerous, not a fix.
In a safety-critical system scores must be trustworthy enough for fail-safe, so 'just ignore it' is unacceptable.

termDefinitions.meaning: 让预测分数等于真实正确概率:0.8 分的检测里约 80% 真的对。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Calibration makes predicted scores equal true correctness probability, so about 80% of detections at 0.8 are actually correct.

termDefinitions.meaning: 对不存在的目标误报导致车辆无故急刹,危险且伤乘坐体验。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Phantom braking is a sudden brake triggered by a false positive on a nonexistent object, dangerous and jarring.

termDefinitions.meaning: 检出了实际不存在的目标。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A false positive is detecting an object that isn't actually there.

q: 补全'校准良好'的数学定义：
q_en: Fill in the definition of well-calibrated confidence:
text: 一个校准良好的检测器满足 P(正确 | 置信度=p) = {{p}}:在置信度 {{0.8}} 的所有检测里,大约 {{80%}} 真的正确。
text_en: A well-calibrated detector satisfies P(correct | confidence=p) = {{p}}: among all detections at {{0.8}} confidence, about {{80%}} are truly correct.
why: 校准的意思是分数就是真实正确概率:0.8 分那批里约 80% 对,0.3 分那批里约 30% 对。这不是准确率指标,而是分数可信度指标——只有校准好,下游的安全阈值才有一致含义。
why_en: Calibration means the score equals the true correctness probability: about 80% of 0.8-score detections are right and about 30% of 0.3-score ones are, and this measures score trustworthiness, not accuracy, so safety thresholds only mean something when scores are calibrated.

termDefinitions.meaning: 预测置信度等于真实正确概率的性质,P(正确|p)=p。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Calibration is the property that predicted confidence equals true correctness probability, P(correct|p)=p.

q: 温度缩放(temperature scaling)怎么校准置信度,代价有多大？
q_en: How does temperature scaling calibrate confidence, and what does it cost?
why: 温度缩放在留出验证集上学一个标量 T,softmax 前把 logits 除以 T:T>1 把过度自信的分数摊平、拉向中间,让分数更接近真实概率。它只是单调缩放,不改预测排序(谁是最高分不变),推理时几乎零成本,是最先试的校准法。
why_en: Temperature scaling learns a single scalar T on held-out validation and divides logits by T before softmax, so T>1 spreads out overconfident scores toward the middle to match true probability, and because it's a monotone rescale it doesn't change the ranking of predictions and adds essentially zero inference cost, making it the first calibration method to try.
options: 重新训练整个检测器让它输出校准分数,推理成本翻倍
给每个类别单独学一个神经网络来重打分,推理明显变慢
在验证集上学单个标量 T,softmax 前缩放 logits,不改排序,推理近零成本
直接把所有置信度截断到 0.5 以上,低于的丢弃
options_en: Retrain the entire detector to output calibrated scores, doubling inference cost.
Learn a separate neural network per class to rescore, noticeably slowing inference.
Learn a single scalar T on validation and rescale logits before softmax, keeping ranking with near-zero inference cost.
Clip all confidences to above 0.5 and discard anything below.
optionExplanations: 温度缩放不重训模型,只学一个标量,推理开销可忽略,不是翻倍。
它就一个全局标量 T,不是每类一个网络,正因如此才近零成本。
对;单标量、softmax 前缩放、保排序、零成本,这四点正是它被优先采用的原因。
截断阈值不是校准,改变不了分数与概率的脱钩,还会误伤低分真目标。
optionExplanations_en: Temperature scaling doesn't retrain the model, just learns one scalar with negligible inference overhead, not double.
It's a single global scalar T, not a per-class network, which is exactly why it's near-zero cost.
Correct — one scalar, rescale before softmax, ranking preserved, zero cost: the four reasons it's the go-to.
Clipping a threshold isn't calibration, doesn't fix the score-probability mismatch, and drops low-score true objects.

termDefinitions.meaning: 校准法:softmax 前把 logits 除以学到的标量 T,摊平过度自信,不改排序。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Temperature scaling divides logits by a learned scalar T before softmax to flatten overconfidence without changing ranking.

termDefinitions.meaning: softmax 之前的原始分数,缩放它等价于调节输出概率的尖锐程度。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Logits are the raw pre-softmax scores; scaling them adjusts how sharp the output probabilities are.

termDefinitions.meaning: 训练时不用、专门用来学 T 的独立数据,防止过拟合。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Held-out validation is data unused in training, reserved for fitting T to avoid overfitting.

scenario: 压缩后的车载检测器整体过度自信,需要校准置信度,但推理预算已经很紧、也不能改变谁是最高分预测。
scenario_en: A compressed on-board detector is broadly overconfident and needs calibration, but the inference budget is tight and the top prediction's ranking must not change.
q: 该优先用哪种校准方法？
q_en: Which calibration method should you reach for first?
why: 预算紧 + 要保排序,首选温度缩放:一个标量 T、softmax 前缩放、推理近零成本,又是单调变换不改排序。若单个 T 不足以修好(比如不同置信区间偏差方向不同),再上 Platt scaling 或 isotonic regression 这类更灵活但更重的方法。
why_en: With a tight budget and ranking to preserve, reach for temperature scaling first: a single scalar T rescaled before softmax at near-zero inference cost and monotone so ranking is untouched, and only if one T isn't enough (e.g. bias differs across confidence bands) move to Platt scaling or isotonic regression.
tradeoff: 温度缩放的零成本单标量 vs Platt/isotonic 的更灵活但更重
whenOtherWins: 当一个全局 T 修不平(不同分段过/欠自信方向不一致)时,Platt scaling 或 isotonic regression 的逐段拟合更合适。
options: 重训整个检测器加校准损失,反正精度也能顺便提
温度缩放:单标量 T、softmax 前缩放、近零成本、不改排序,正合预算与保序要求
Platt scaling:上来就用最灵活的,免得以后不够用
直接把阈值从 0.5 提到 0.9,不做任何校准
options_en: Retrain the whole detector with a calibration loss, since it might improve accuracy too.
Temperature scaling — single scalar T, rescale before softmax, near-zero cost, ranking preserved, matching the budget and ordering needs.
Platt scaling — start with the most flexible method so you never run short later.
Just raise the threshold from 0.5 to 0.9 without any calibration.
optionExplanations: 重训贵、慢,还可能动排序,预算紧时是最后手段而非首选。
对;温度缩放正好命中'零成本'和'不改排序'两个约束,是该先试的校准法。
Platt 更重、可能改排序,单个 T 够用时先上它是过度工程。
提阈值不是校准,分数与概率脱钩的问题还在,还会漏掉低分真目标。
optionExplanations_en: Retraining is costly, slow, and can shift ranking, so it's a last resort under a tight budget, not first.
Correct — temperature scaling hits both the zero-cost and ranking-preserving constraints, the method to try first.
Platt is heavier and can change ranking, so leading with it when a single T suffices is over-engineering.
Raising the threshold isn't calibration, leaves the score-probability gap, and drops low-score true objects.

termDefinitions.meaning: 用一个逻辑回归把分数映射到校准概率,比单个温度更灵活。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Platt scaling fits a logistic regression to map scores to calibrated probabilities, more flexible than a single temperature.

termDefinitions.meaning: 拟合一个单调非降函数逐段校准分数,灵活但需更多数据。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Isotonic regression fits a monotone non-decreasing function to calibrate scores piecewise, flexible but data-hungry.

termDefinitions.meaning: 单标量 T 缩放 logits,零成本、不改排序的首选校准法。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Temperature scaling rescales logits by a single scalar T, a zero-cost ranking-preserving default calibrator.

q: 以下哪些是置信度校准方法？(多选)
q_en: Which of the following are confidence-calibration methods? (multiple)
why: 温度缩放、Platt scaling、isotonic regression 都是把分数重新映射到真实概率的校准法,复杂度递增。NMS 是检测后处理,去掉重叠冗余框,和把分数变可信没关系,别混进来。
why_en: Temperature scaling, Platt scaling, and isotonic regression all remap scores toward true probability with increasing complexity, while NMS is detection post-processing that removes overlapping duplicate boxes and has nothing to do with making scores trustworthy.
options: 温度缩放(temperature scaling)
Platt scaling
isotonic regression(保序回归)
NMS(非极大值抑制)
options_en: Temperature scaling.
Platt scaling.
Isotonic regression.
NMS (non-maximum suppression).
optionExplanations: 对;单标量 T 缩放 logits,零成本的默认校准法。
对;逻辑回归映射分数,比单个温度灵活,一个 T 不够时用。
对;拟合单调函数逐段校准,最灵活但要更多数据。
错;NMS 是去重叠框的后处理,不改分数与概率的对应关系,不是校准法。
optionExplanations_en: Correct — a single scalar T rescaling logits, the zero-cost default calibrator.
Correct — a logistic mapping of scores, more flexible than one temperature, used when a single T is insufficient.
Correct — fits a monotone function for piecewise calibration, most flexible but data-hungry.
Incorrect — NMS is duplicate-box post-processing that doesn't touch the score-probability mapping, so it isn't calibration.

termDefinitions.meaning: 检测后处理,保留最高分框、抑制与其重叠的冗余框,与校准无关。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: NMS (Non-Maximum Suppression) is post-processing that keeps the top-scoring box and suppresses overlapping duplicates, unrelated to calibration.

termDefinitions.meaning: 拟合单调非降函数校准分数的非参数方法。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Isotonic regression is a non-parametric method fitting a monotone non-decreasing function to calibrate scores.

scenario: 校准后,检测器对前方一个目标只给出低于安全阈值的置信度,系统必须决定怎么动作。
scenario_en: After calibration, the detector gives a below-safety-threshold confidence to an object ahead, and the system must decide how to act.
q: 校准好的置信度在 fail-safe 设计里该怎么用？
q_en: How should calibrated confidence feed a fail-safe design?
why: 校准让分数可信后,fail-safe 用它做门:置信度低于安全阈值时,不拿这个不可靠检测直接决策,而是走保守回退——降速、提醒人类操作员接管。核心是宁可保守也不基于不可信的检测贸然行动,这在安全攸关系统里是非可选项。
why_en: Once calibration makes scores trustworthy, fail-safe uses them as a gate: when confidence falls below a safety threshold, don't act on that unreliable detection but take a conservative fallback — slow down and alert a human operator — because acting conservatively beats acting on untrustworthy detections, a non-negotiable in safety-critical systems.
diagram:
flowchart TB
  D["校准后置信度"] --> Q{"低于安全阈值?"}
  Q -->|否| A["正常决策"]
  Q -->|是| F["回退:降速+提醒操作员"]
options: 低于安全阈值→保守回退(降速、提醒人类操作员),不拿不可靠检测直接决策
低于阈值就直接忽略该目标,当作没看到继续原速行驶
低于阈值反而更该相信,置信度低说明目标罕见更危险,应加速通过
校准分数只用于离线报表,实时决策不看置信度
options_en: Below the safety threshold, take a conservative fallback (slow down, alert a human operator) instead of acting on an unreliable detection.
Below the threshold, just ignore the object and keep driving at full speed as if nothing is there.
Below the threshold you should trust it more — low confidence means a rare, more dangerous object, so accelerate through.
Calibrated scores are only for offline reports, and real-time decisions ignore confidence.
optionExplanations: 对;可信的低分触发保守回退,是'宁可降速也不基于不可信检测行动'的 fail-safe 逻辑。
低分直接忽略正是危险行为——那可能是个只给了 0.3 的真行人,忽略等于撞上去。
低置信度不代表更该相信,更不该加速,这与安全逻辑完全相反。
安全攸关系统的实时决策必须用校准置信度做门控,只做报表是浪费了校准的意义。
optionExplanations_en: Correct — a trustworthy low score triggers a conservative fallback, the fail-safe logic of slowing rather than acting on an unreliable detection.
Ignoring low scores is the dangerous move — that could be a real pedestrian scored only 0.3, and ignoring it means hitting them.
Low confidence is no reason to trust more or accelerate; that's the opposite of safety logic.
Real-time decisions in a safety-critical system must gate on calibrated confidence; report-only wastes the point of calibration.

termDefinitions.meaning: 不确定或异常时退到最保守、伤害最小的动作(如降速、交人接管)。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Fail-safe means falling back to the most conservative, least-harmful action under uncertainty, such as slowing or handing off to a human.

termDefinitions.meaning: 校准置信度的下限,低于它就不基于该检测直接决策而触发回退。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A safety threshold is a lower bound on calibrated confidence below which the system takes a fallback instead of acting on the detection.
